userStories.title: Plan validation
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Validate compaction plans deterministically and collect every rejection reason.

**Motivation** — Most are `type: project`, `source: nax-run` notes about a single story ("Applies when extending <file> ... (story 14 onward)") that stop mattering once the feature ships.

**Approach** — `validateMemoryCompactionPlan(plan, candidates, existingSlugs)` collects every reason a plan is invalid (not only the first). `existingSlugs` is every slug a merge target must not take: the caller passes the mirror's project slugs, and the nax host adds the repository notes' slugs. A plan is invalid when any of these holds:

1. It retires nothing and merges nothing.
2. A retire slug or a merge `from` slug is not a candidate.
3. A slug appears in more than one action (two retires, a retire and a merge source, two merges' sources, or two merges' `into.slug`).
4. A merge has fewer than two `from` slugs.
5. A merge's `from` notes are of different types, or `into.type` differs from their type.
6. A merge's `into.slug` is in `existingSlugs` and is not one of that merge's own `from` slugs.
7. A merge's `into` fails `validateMemoryNoteWrite` (scope `project`, source `MEMORY_COMPACTION_SOURCE`), which covers the slug pattern, the 200-character description, the 8192-byte body and the secret scan.
8. A retire reason fails `forgetReasonRefusal` (one line, at most 200 characters, not empty).

**Scope** — In: validator in upstream compaction-plan.ts, memory/internal exports and regenerated API snapshot. Out: model parsing (US-011), locked revalidation (US-003), host reserved-slug plumbing (US-012). No cap on how many candidates one plan may retire; the archive and `nax memory undo` are the safety net.

**Interface** —
```typescript
export function validateMemoryCompactionPlan(
  plan: MemoryCompactionPlan,
  candidates: readonly MemoryNote[],
  existingSlugs: ReadonlySet<string>,
): MemoryCompactionPlanCheck;
```

userStories.title: Apply rollback, archive retention and ordering
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make failed apply restore the mirror/outbox, retain recoverable archives and serialize competing applies.

**Motivation** — When the rendered index passes its cap, `renderMemoryIndex` drops entries off the end and reports only a count (`RenderedMemoryIndex.omitted`) that no caller reads, so a session silently loses notes.

**Approach** — Rollback: when any of steps 4-8 throws, the apply deletes each merged note it wrote whose slug is not an archived original, writes every archived original back, removes every outbox entry it enqueued (`outbox.remove(clientId)`), rewrites the manifest with `status: "rolled_back"`, refreshes the index, and throws `MEMORY_COMPACT_FAILED` with the original error as `cause`.

9. Outside the lock: among the archive directories whose name matches `MEMORY_COMPACTION_ID_RE` and whose manifest has `status: "applied"`, delete all but the newest `keepArchives` (by id order). The compaction just written is always kept; an `applying` or `rolled_back` archive, and any directory not named like an id, is never deleted and never counts toward the limit.

Failure behavior: writing the archive fails -> `MEMORY_COMPACT_FAILED`, no note changed. A note write, delete, enqueue, index refresh, manifest or log write fails -> Rollback (see Atomic apply), manifest `rolled_back`, `MEMORY_COMPACT_FAILED` with `cause`. The rollback itself throws -> `logger.error`, still `MEMORY_COMPACT_FAILED` with the original `cause` and context `rollback: "incomplete"`. Deleting an old archive fails -> `logger.warn`, the compaction still succeeds.

**Scope** — In: rollback, fault translation, archive retention and concurrent-apply ordering in upstream apply/archive modules. Out: undo (US-006..007), host provider sync (US-012). `rolled_back` and `applying` archive directories are never pruned automatically; they stay until removed by hand or by `nax memory mirrors --prune` removing the whole mirror. A compaction or undo waits for another process's mirror lock exactly as any writer does; only a sync in flight in this process is refused with `MEMORY_BUSY`.

**Interface** —
```typescript
export function applyMemoryCompaction(input: MemoryCompactionApplyInput): Promise<MemoryCompactionResult>;
```
Continue using the upstream input's keepArchives, logger, now, timers and isAlive seams; rollback removes only entries this apply enqueued and never touches unrelated outbox entries. A rolled-back apply leaves no compactionsLog line for its id, including when the append failed after writing bytes; preserve earlier log lines when cleaning that failed record.

userStories.title: MEMORY_FULL save guard
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Refuse a new scoped slug before staging when the host's optional index projection would omit entries.

**Motivation** — When the rendered index passes its cap, `renderMemoryIndex` drops entries off the end and reports only a count (`RenderedMemoryIndex.omitted`) that no caller reads, so a session silently loses notes.

**Approach** — `MemorySaveInput` gains an optional `indexOverflows(note)` hook. `saveMemoryNote` calls it under the lock only when the mirror holds no note under the write's key (a new slug). When it answers true, the save is refused with `NaxError` code `MEMORY_FULL` and nothing is staged, queued or pushed. Overwriting an existing slug is always allowed.

The nax-agent message is generic (`memory index is full: a new note would drop entries from the index`); the nax tool result adds the hint `run nax memory compact, or overwrite an existing note`. In chat and runs the memory tool's result carries the refusal, so the agent can tell the user.

**Scope** — In: optional hook in operations-support.ts MemorySaveInput and guard in operations.ts deliverLocked before any mirror/outbox/provider mutation. Out: host index projection and tool hint (US-012), run refusal counting (US-019), compaction itself (US-003..005). The `MEMORY_FULL` guard covers saves only: `nax memory approve` putting a pending note in force, notes a sync pulls from koda, and repository notes are not refused, and can still push the index past its cap. US-008 only: a save fenced by a sync in flight in this process (queued without staging) is not checked by `indexOverflows`.

**Interface** — `MemorySaveInput` remains `MemoryOperationInput & { write, writeMode, source }`, plus:
```typescript
readonly indexOverflows?: (note: MemoryNote) => Promise<boolean>;
```
The callback receives the actual staged-note shape, including generated id, status, source and clock timestamp. Existing callers without the optional hook retain today's behavior.

userStories.title: memory.compact config and fill
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add typed compaction configuration and pure rendered-index fullness measurement.

**Motivation** — Survey of `~/.nax/memory/projects/` on 2026-11-25: the largest mirror holds 115 notes and its index is at 90% of the 24576-byte cap; three more sit at 58-70%.

**Approach** — Fill = `max(bytes / memory.indexBytes, lines / MEMORY_INDEX_MAX_LINES)` over the text of `MemoryHost.renderIndex()`. Bytes are the UTF-8 byte length; lines are the newline-separated line count, 0 for empty text. `memory.indexBytes` is the configured value (default 24576), not the `MEMORY_INDEX_MAX_BYTES` constant.

Nearly full = `RenderedMemoryIndex.omitted > 0` **or** fill >= `memory.compact.threshold` (default 0.8). The `omitted` test is applied first: an index with omitted entries is nearly full even when its fill is below the threshold.

Displayed percentages are `Math.round(fill * 100)`.

`MemoryConfigSchema` gains `compact`: a strict object defaulting to `{}` with `threshold` (number, > 0 and <= 1, default `0.8`), `model` (`ConfiguredModelSchema`, default `"balanced"`) and `keepArchives` (integer 1-50, default `5`). The hand-written `MemoryConfig` interface, used by `NaxConfig.memory`, gains `compact: { threshold: number; model: ConfiguredModel; keepArchives: number }`.

**Scope** — In: schemas-memory.ts, runtime-types-memory.ts, config-descriptions.ts, fill.ts, memory barrel exports, existing DEFAULT_MEMORY fixture replacement and the hand-written resolved-config fixture in schemas-memory.test.ts. Preserve memoryConfigOf's pass-through of an already resolved block; add compact to that fixture rather than re-parsing configured memory at runtime. Out: model operation (US-011), host guard (US-012), chat/run triggering (US-017/019). `nax memory status` does not gain fill or last-compaction fields.

**Interface** —
```typescript
export function memoryIndexFill(index: RenderedMemoryIndex, indexBytes: number): number;
export function memoryNearlyFull(index: RenderedMemoryIndex, memory: MemoryConfig): boolean;
```
Update the closed DEFAULT_MEMORY literals in schemas-memory.test.ts with `compact: { threshold: 0.8, model: "balanced", keepArchives: 5 }`, preserving existing schema/default assertions.

userStories.title: Host compaction members and the full-index hook
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Compose agent compaction/undo and an exact overflow projection into every memory host.

**Motivation** — When the rendered index passes its cap, `renderMemoryIndex` drops entries off the end and reports only a count (`RenderedMemoryIndex.omitted`) that no caller reads, so a session silently loses notes.

**Approach** — `host.ts` is at 581 of its 600 lines and must stay at or under 600: the new members and their input/result types are declared and implemented in a new `packages/nax/src/memory/host-compact.ts` as a factory `createHostCompaction({ store, outbox, logger, config, providerId, writeMode, repoNotes, sync, operations })` that `createMemoryHost` calls with `_memoryHostDeps` as `operations`, exactly as it calls `createHostWrites` (so `host-compact.ts` never imports `host.ts` and no import cycle forms), and `readIndex` (`host.ts:496-504`) moves to a new `packages/nax/src/memory/host-index.ts` so the index render is shared by `renderIndex` and the `indexOverflows` hook.

The nax host supplies the hook: it renders the host index exactly as `renderIndex` does (both scopes, decisions, repository notes, pending notes shown as today) with the new note added to its own scope's list (a new project note whose slug a repository note holds replaces that repository note in the projection, as the mirror's note shadows it in `renderIndex`), and answers `omitted > 0`. The closure is built in `host-index.ts` next to the moved `readIndex`.

Writes are mirror + outbox only, exactly as a direct save or forget stages them. Delivery to a remote provider is the existing sync: the nax host runs one `sync()` after the apply (US-012). A post-apply sync throw logs logger.warn; the compaction result stands. Undo also syncs once after successful staging. The host passes repository note slugs as reservedSlugs and keepArchives from resolved config.

`HostWritesInput` gains `readonly indexOverflows: (note: MemoryNote) => Promise<boolean>`, and `save` passes it to `saveMemoryNote`. A `MEMORY_FULL` error becomes `{ isError: true, content: "[memory] save refused: <message>; run nax memory compact, or overwrite an existing note" }`, the shape `MEMORY_WRITE_REFUSED` takes plus the hint.

`memory.writeMode` is `"proposal"` -> The host refuses with `MEMORY_COMPACT_UNSUPPORTED`; `compactProjectMemory` returns `unsupported` before any model call; the CLI prints `Error: memory compaction is not available with memory.writeMode "proposal"; nothing was changed` and exits 1. Both apply and undo are unsupported in proposal mode.

**Scope** — In: host-compact.ts factory/types, host-index.ts shared reads/projection, optional MemoryHost members, _memoryHostDeps apply/undo seams, host-writes hook and tool-provider failure message. Out: apply/undo internals (US-003..008), orchestration (US-014), origin side effect (US-020). The `MEMORY_FULL` guard covers saves only: `nax memory approve` putting a pending note in force, notes a sync pulls from koda, and repository notes are not refused, and can still push the index past its cap. Compaction and undo under `memory.writeMode: "proposal"` are refused as unsupported; a proposal-mode compaction (every change held for approval) is not built.

**Interface** — MemoryHost gains these optional members; _memoryHostDeps gains applyMemoryCompaction and undoMemoryCompaction:
```typescript
compactionCandidates?(): Promise<readonly MemoryNote[]>;
applyCompaction?(input: { readonly plan: MemoryCompactionPlan; readonly model: string; readonly fillBefore: number }): Promise<MemoryCompactionResult>;
undoCompaction?(input: { readonly id?: string; readonly force?: boolean }): Promise<MemoryUndoResult>;
```
Implement their factory in host-compact.ts and use internal agent exports; do not extend the capped agent root entry.
